sections.html:
Lake County divides property tax between two desks. One sets the worth of each parcel and files exemptions. The other prints the bill and takes the money. A problem with value belongs to the first and a problem with payment to the second, and neither can repair the other's side.

To fix a name, mailing address, parcel location or assessed value, phone the Property Appraiser at (352) 253-2150. Bills open for collection on November 1, and a notice lost in the mail does not excuse a late payment. Escrowed loans are marked with a code at the top of the notice and a banner along the bottom.

  • Property Appraiser: assigns values, processes homestead and other exemptions, sends the proposed-tax notice in August.
  • Tax Collector: mails bills, receives payments, and holds the June certificate sale for accounts still open.
  • Clerk of the Circuit Court: records the deed, takes in the stamp tax, and staffs the value adjustment board.

An owner who pays in November saves up to 4 percent. Each later month trims one point off that saving until February, and from March there is nothing to claim.

Lake County payment schedule for the full annual bill
Paid in full byDiscount
November 304 percent
December 313 percent
January 312 percent
February 281 percent
March 31Gross amount, no discount

For mailed checks the postmark decides which discount applies. Come April 1, a statutory 3 percent interest charge joins the balance, and unpaid items head toward the certificate sale by June 1.

Installment terms and the sale calendar are fixed by the collector yearly. Phone that office before planning around either.

sections.h2: What millage rates apply to a Lake County home?
sections.html:
The answer changes with location. The 2026 final millage rate sheet from the appraiser gives one total for each taxing district code, from the low 13s in unincorporated land up to the high 19s in some cities.

The unincorporated codes at the top of the sheet total 13.0632, 13.0670 or 13.4678, depending on the code. Three lines repeat in every row: the county general fund at 5.0254, the school board state line at 3.0560 and the school board local line at 2.9980. What separates one district from another is the extra layers, such as a city levy, a fire or ambulance district, a hospital district or a community development district.

  • Clermont: 16.2875 total, with a city line of 4.2000.
  • Leesburg: 15.8704 total, with a city line of 3.3783.
  • Mount Dora: 18.7921 total, with a city line of 6.3000.
  • Eustis: 19.8819 total, with a city line of 7.3898.
  • Montverde: 15.3975 total, with a city line of 2.8300.

Your code appears on your notice and on the parcel record; match it to its row on the sheet. The cities on the sheet are Astatula, Clermont, Eustis, Fruitland Park, Groveland, Howey-in-the-Hills, Lady Lake, Leesburg, Mascotte, Minneola, Montverde, Mount Dora, Tavares and Umatilla.

sections.h2: Homestead exemption and Save Our Homes
sections.html:
Making the house your residence by January 1 and filing before March 1 exempts as much as $50,000 of value. School levies reach only the first slice of that exemption, so the school lines on the millage sheet (3.0560 and 2.9980) get the smaller break.

The application is Form DR-501, filed with the appraiser. Leasing the home out or moving away ends the benefit. Extra senior, veteran and disability breaks may exist locally, and the appraiser's home page links to a list of them with eligibility rules.

Save Our Homes caps how fast a homestead's assessment can climb, tying the ceiling to inflation. The state chart lists 2.7 percent for 2026, 2.9 percent for 2025 and 3.0 percent for 2024. Once the house sells, the parcel is assessed at market value again, and the buyer's first full bill can differ sharply from yours. If you are buying another Florida home, portability may let you bring the accumulated savings along; it uses a separate form and a three-year window.

The settlement statement splits this year's tax between you and the buyer. Older unpaid years have to be settled before title moves, and the title company typically sends the collector that money out of what the seller would receive.

No statement exists yet for the current year when a house sells in spring or summer, so the title agent estimates it. Ask the collector for the exact number and for any older balance while terms are still being worked out.

  • Check the parcel record for the right owner name and mailing address.
  • Ask the collector if any year is delinquent or has been sold as a certificate.
  • Mention your homestead exemption to the title company so the split uses the correct amount.
  • Request a draft settlement statement early and check its tax line against what the collector told you.
  • Tell the buyer that the next bill may be higher once the value resets.

State law sets deed stamps at 70 cents for each $100 of consideration. The contract may name a payer, yet both parties stay liable.

A bill still open on April 1 is delinquent, and the parcel can in time reach a tax deed sale. Before that it is sold as a certificate, and the holder must wait two years before asking for a deed.

The certificate sale opens on or before June 1. Bidders compete by taking the lowest interest rate, and certificates nobody wants go to the county. Homestead parcels owing under $250 are issued to the county without an auction. When a deed sale does happen, the clerk holds a public auction and the high bidder leaves a nonrefundable deposit.

Owners who cannot pay may qualify for deferral. A homestead owner with a low income can ask the collector to put off part of the bill using Form DR-570, due at the end of March. The installment prepayment request has its own May 1 date.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Lake County value?
sections.html:
When the August notice shows a value you dispute, you have 25 days from the notice to petition the value adjustment board. Count from the date printed on it, not the day it arrived.

If an exemption or deferral is denied, a separate 30-day clock starts on the day the denial letter was mailed. The clerk's office supports the board and posts its forms. Speak with the appraiser first; questions about square footage or exemption status often get resolved without a petition.

Before you call, gather the notice, recent nearby sales, photos and any repair estimates. Those are the papers the appraiser will want to see.

Budget hearings by the taxing authorities take place in September and October, with final millage following. Rates are argued there, while your own house's value is argued with the appraiser.

faqs.q: When are Lake County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Pay in November for 4 percent off, with the discount shrinking to 1 percent in February. The full amount is due by the end of March, and a 3 percent charge applies from April 1.

faqs.q: Who do I call to change my Lake County mailing address on a tax bill?
faqs.a: Phone the Lake County Property Appraiser at (352) 253-2150. The collector cannot alter a name, address, location or assessed value.

faqs.q: What is the total millage in unincorporated Lake County?
faqs.a: Unincorporated codes total 13.0632, 13.0670 or 13.4678 on the 2026 final sheet, depending on district. Find your code on your notice.

faqs.q: Does selling my Lake County house reset my tax value?
faqs.a: For the buyer, yes. Your capped value stays behind because the sale is a change of ownership.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lake County house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance and any certificate redemption are paid from your proceeds. Obtain a payoff from the collector and hand it to the closing agent early.
